headline: Not a collapse — read the pipeline, not the newest row: 9 of Ep 21's 11 shorts are still scheduled-private (Nov 8–16, one publishAt per day) and show 0 because they haven't aired yet, and the last 2–3 days of every pull lag the Analytics API by design, so the newest videos always look dead for a day or two. The real week (10/30–11/5, the last with full data) was the channel's best in a month: 2,661 views vs 1,602 (Oct 23 wk) and 1,279 (Oct 16 wk), subs 31→34, driven by two shorts breaking out — 'Don't Tell Claude About the PHP Bug' (549 engaged) and 'Your iPhone PIN Is More Secure Than This Root CA' (322). Long-form CTR is fine on both (Ep 20 3.63%, Ep 21 3.67%) but Ep 21 never got Ep 20's launch-week impression push — rebuilding the daily Reporting API series shows Ep 20's first 3 days ran 456/121/436/398 (1,013 total) while Ep 21's ran flat and low from day 0 (80/124/98..., 302 in 3 days, 30% of Ep 20's) — likely the Oct 26 rebrand re-indexing the channel, Ep 21's own retention collapse (below) throttling distribution in real time, or both; Ep 22's launch trajectory is the next clean read. The one genuine new red flag: Ep 21's retention cratered to 5.7% at the 10% mark, the worst on record (vs the 14–24% Ep 15–20 band), because the edit stacked a housekeeping chapter (the rebrand announcement at 0:50) directly in front of the perp pick (2:15) before the Binance hook ever lands (4:36) — two of the three worst-scoring opening moves on the show, back to back. Shorts: Ep 20's batch of 13 broke the Oct 10–20 collapse partially (2/13 cleared 250 views = 15%, up from 0/16, still under the 31% base rate), and the 2 winners were concrete-object/security titles (PHP bug, root CA) while the back half of the same batch (perp/insider-jargon titles: Hyperliquid, 'dumb contract', 'hack the university') went back to flopping at 2–20 views — same pattern as always, not a platform-wide drop.

production.title: Scheduled-private videos reading as zero views is pipeline lag, not underperformance — don't re-litigate this weekly
production.evidence: 9 of Ep 21's 11 shorts (queued 'Negative Alpha Is Also Alpha' through 'We Had No Bitcoin Flip and Still Made $2.67') are privacyStatus=private with publishAt 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-16 — they have never been public, so reach/engaged_views are null by construction. The 2 that are already public ('Live From a Bathroom...' 11/6, 'Binance Got Hacked for Five B-illions' 11/7) are 1–2 days old; the Analytics API's daily series in this pull only covers through 2026-11-05, so anything published after that has no data yet regardless of real performance.
production.recommendation: No action — this is expected. When a weekly pull lands right after a publish burst, grade the LAST complete week (data through day-2) and treat anything newer as 'too early,' not 'underperforming.'
production.status_note: documented 11/8 after it read as a false alarm.

production.title: Shorts feed: partial recovery, not a fix — winner-template titles still the only ones that clear 250 views
production.evidence: Ep 20's 13-short batch (10/24–11/5, 1/day): 2 of 13 broke out — 'Don't Tell Claude About the PHP Bug' 549 engaged, 'Your iPhone PIN Is More Secure Than This Root CA' 322 — both concrete-object + security/absurd titles, same shape as every historical breakout. The other 11 (incl. perp/insider titles 'Hyperliquid's Nodes Are in His Basement' 20, '"So It Was a Dumb Contract"' 2, 'Hack the University for the Test Answers' 3, '"Guess Who's Out of the Permanent Underclass"' 8, 'Vitalik Built Plato's Cave for AI Agents' 14) stayed in single/low-double digits. 2/13 = 15%, up from the Oct 10–20 collapse (0/16) but still below the Sep 1 base rate (31%, 14/45).
production.recommendation: Keep the winner template (concrete object, dollar figure, or security/hack angle) and keep cutting perp-pick and insider-jargon shorts even when the segment itself played well live. Ep 21's 11-short batch (going out Nov 8–16, one a day) is the next read — grade it the same way once it clears the 3-day window per clip.

production.title: CTR is fine, but Ep 21 never got the launch-week impression push Ep 19/20 got — rebuilt the day-by-day series to check, and it's real
production.evidence: Launch CTR looks fine on both (Ep 20 3.63%, Ep 21 3.67%) but CTR is only half the story — total launch-week reach is impressions × CTR, and impressions themselves diverged hard. Rebuilt per-video daily impressions from the Reporting API (channel_reach_basic_a1, bypassing the sliding-window gotcha): Ep 20's first 3 days ran 456 / 121 / 436 / 398 (day 0–3, a real sustained push, 1,013 total). Ep 21's first 3 days ran 80 / 124 / 98 / 37 / 64 / 70 / 45 (day 0–6) — flat and low from the very first day, never pushed, 302 in the first 3 days (30% of Ep 20's). This is not a day-count artifact (Ep 20's own day-0 alone, 456, already beats Ep 21's best single day, 124) and it isn't a CTR problem (Ep 21's CTR on the impressions it did get was as good as Ep 20's). Two live hypotheses, not mutually exclusive: (1) the Oct 26 channel rebrand (name change jacksoncook → Underpod) landed 4 days before Ep 21 published and can cause YouTube's recommender to temporarily under-distribute a newly-renamed channel while it re-indexes identity signals; (2) Ep 21's catastrophic early retention (5.7% at the 10% mark, see recording items) may have throttled further suggested/browse distribution within hours of publish — YouTube's recommender reacts to session data in near-real-time, not just at day boundaries.
production.recommendation: n=1 post-rebrand episode, so don't overfit yet. Ep 22's day 0–3 impressions (not yet in this pull — published 11/6) is the next clean read: if it shows Ep 20's shape (a real push), Ep 21 was a one-off, most likely explained by its own retention collapse. If Ep 22 is also flat like Ep 21, that points at something systemic post-rebrand (channel re-indexing, or the standalone/shorts cadence cannibalizing suggested slots) and is worth a direct look at Studio's 'impressions by source' chart for Ep 22 vs Ep 20.
production.status_note: new 11/8, built by rebuilding the Reporting API's per-video daily series instead of reading the lifetime `reach` field.

production.title: Underpod Explains (standalones): 2 of 13 live, and neither is ranking in search yet — the entire bet behind the series hasn't shown up
production.evidence: Per-video traffic-source pull on the 2 live standalones: 'How the Lightning Network actually works' (10/28) — 40 of 45 views (89%) from SUBSCRIBER, 4 from YT_SEARCH; 'Will quantum computers break Bitcoin?' (11/4) — 32 of 48 views (67%) from SUBSCRIBER, 3 from YT_SEARCH. The standalones plan's whole thesis (episodes/standalones.md) was that search-intent titles would pull incremental search traffic the regular episodes don't get (search is the channel's #2 source lifetime, 2,008 views, but mostly novelty queries). Right now these two are behaving exactly like small episode clips — subscriber-fed, low-view — not like search assets. CTR is also lower than episodes (1.94% / 1.2% vs 3.6%+), consistent with a quiet Tuesday slot and no launch push, which is expected for this format. One real positive: avg-view% is much higher than episodes (23.35% / 15.88% vs 7–10%) — people who do land on them watch more, which is the right signal if search traffic eventually arrives.
production.recommendation: Too early to call — SEO ranking typically takes months, not two weeks, and 11 more are scheduled through 2027-01-19. Don't read the low view counts as a failure yet, but don't count the search thesis as validated either. Re-check traffic source (not just view count) at the 8-week mark once 6–8 are live; if SUBSCRIBER still dominates then with near-zero YT_SEARCH, the format isn't doing what it was built for and the cadence should be reconsidered.
production.status_note: new 11/8; first per-video traffic-source check on the series.

recording.title: Ep 21 posted the worst opening on record (5.7% at the 10% mark) by stacking a housekeeping beat in front of the perp pick, both before the hook
recording.evidence: study.md §8: Ep 21's first 10% (≈5:39 of 56:34) runs cold open (45s) → 'The Permanent Underpod is dead: the rebrand' (0:50, housekeeping) → Perp of Fortune (2:15) → the Binance hook doesn't land until 4:36. vs_typ at the 10% mark is 0.06 — essentially bottom-of-the-curve. Compare Ep 20, which kept perp near the top but without a housekeeping beat in front of it and got the best 10%-mark retention since Ep 15 (19.1%, vs_typ 0.40). Launch CTR for Ep 21 was still 3.67% (strong), confirming this is a pure post-click retention failure, not a packaging one.
recording.recommendation: Treat any housekeeping/announcement beat (rebrand news, show updates) exactly like banter: never cold-open into one, push it past the first third. Keep running the perp pick as the first break around minute 8–10, after the marquee hook, per the existing §1 recommendation — Ep 21 moved it earlier instead of later and the two together did more damage than either alone.

recording.title: Ep 20 confirms: moving the hook earlier (even without fully deferring perp) lifts the 10%-mark number
recording.evidence: Ep 15–19 10%-mark retention: 24.6 / 17.4 / 14.3 / 16.2 / 15.7. Ep 20: 19.1 — second-best of the six perp-adjacent-opening episodes, achieved by landing the marquee hook sooner even though perp still sat near the top.
recording.recommendation: Keep tightening the gap between cold open and the marquee hook; full confirmation of 'perp at minute 8–10' is still pending a clean test (no episode has tried it yet) — Ep 22 or 23 should be the one.
